_about: Registry of Enigma machines and cipher stations in the Spanish theatre (Caja 745 context). Two INDEPENDENT axes: machine TYPE (chassis/family) and WIRING (rotor Schaltung, named by German phonetic alphabet). Fill in as archive material appears. Keep 'source' and 'confidence' on every row (data vs inference).

_schema.serial: machine serial if known (e.g. A1236, A17316S); else null
_schema.type: one of: commercial_unsteckered | funkschluessel_M | legion_condor_numbered | unknown
_schema.plugboard: true/false (commercial family = false; M and Condor variant = true)
_schema.wiring: rotor wiring nickname: D (Dora) | F (Friedrich) | C (Caesar, unpublished target) | unknown
_schema.digits_on_rotors: true only for the Legion Condor variant (numbers instead of letters)
_schema.holder: unit / service that held or used it

wiring_nicknames.C: Caesar  -- unpublished; the recovery target for DHZB/LUIS
wiring_nicknames.D: Dora    -- Schaltung D; commercial unsteckered machines; also Italian Army/Navy (Soler 2010)
wiring_nicknames.F: Friedrich -- the wiring of the XMOT message (certified)
wiring_nicknames._note: these label ROTOR WIRINGS, not machine models; do not confuse Schaltung D with reflector UKW D

machine_types.commercial_unsteckered: commercial Enigma (D/K family), no plugboard, QWERTZ ETW -- the SPANISH/Italian machines ('Dora'); the toolkit's domain
machine_types.funkschluessel_M: Kriegsmarine naval Enigma M, plugboard, letters on rotors -- German only
machine_types.legion_condor_numbered: 'same principle as Funkschluessel M but NUMBERS on the rotors instead of letters' -- German (Legion Condor), plugboard

machines.notes: wired with Dora (D); likely the whole A123x group shares it
three-wheel Heeres-type, specially wired -- NOT the commercial family
one exemplar exchanged at a warship/Dv. Nord; to be returned to the Kriegsmarine after Uebung Hansa
'same principle as Funkschluessel M but numbers on the rotors instead of letters'; returned per Legion Condor instructions
the 'Dora' machines of the return order; commercial unsteckered, wiring D
XMOT breaks with wiring F, order II-I-III, windows TXMO
does not break with D or F -> working hypothesis: Caesar (C), unpublished. RECOVERY TARGET.

entities.Dienststelle Sander: German office (K.K. Wagner - Meyer Doehner) that set up the 3-language DEI signal procedure + Enigma, early 1937
German naval command in Spain (Befehlshaber der Spanien-gewaesser)
entities.Partner: codename for the Spanish naval service -- the intermediary that received the machines
entities.Sonderstab W: special staff W (clears value/return of the material)
entities.Gruppe Nordsee: German naval group that used M + Legion Condor Enigmas
entities.Legion Condor: German air/naval expeditionary force; first Enigmas came to Spain with it
entities.DEI: Deutschland-Espana-Italia -- the joint reconnaissance signal table / codebook (early 1937)

sources.desc: German Seekriegsleitung file on Spanish-theatre radio/cipher material return (1937-1939); folios 24, 29/120, 108-109, 118 seen so far
sources.archive: US NARA microfilm T1022 (German Navy records)
